question: What are your principles of product management? How do you mentor other PMs on how to get stuff done?
competency: Hire and Develop the Best (mentoring, coaching)

raiseTranscript.text: I focus on customer problems first, then work backward from the data. One principle is to always validate assumptions with at least two sources before committing to a roadmap. For mentoring, I pair with new PMs on writing PRDs and give feedback on clarity.
How did you apply that with a peer?
I sat with a new PM who kept adding features without metrics. We rewrote one spec together and added success criteria; their next launch hit the target.

junior.raiseFeedback: Raises the bar for junior. Competency is Hire and Develop the Best. Story centered on validating assumptions with two data sources and rewriting a spec with a peer PM so the launch hit its target metric. This shows ownership of their own work plus willingness to help others improve. The example is small in scope but demonstrates coachability and concrete feedback delivery. Biggest strength is grounding principles in repeatable actions rather than platitudes.

One PM reduced scope by 30% after we added outcome metrics; the other team shipped two weeks early and the metric moved 8%.

raiseTranscript.text: Principles are outcome over output, clear ownership, and building a learning culture. I mentor by running a monthly PM guild where we review underperforming launches and assign coaches to struggling PMs.
How did you handle one underperformer?
A PM kept missing deadlines. We paired them with a senior peer for two sprints, reset expectations on scoping, and their on-time rate went from 40% to 85%.

raiseTranscript.text: My principles are long-term platform bets over short-term features, building a talent bench, and making trade-offs visible to the business. I mentor by creating a PM leadership program that rotates high-potentials across orgs and tracks their promotion rates.
After two years the program produced four directors; two of them drove platform launches that reduced infrastructure costs 22% while increasing release velocity.
